primitives.name: Disagreement Abstention Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT The disagreement-based abstention construction (abstain exactly where near-optimal policies disagree) and the abstention-powered safe-policy-improvement protocol are both directly adaptable: the first to GSE's post/no-post decision, the second to certifying engine version upgrades before public deployment.
primitives.assumptions: Binary treatment space, unknown propensities, bounded rewards, stable observational distribution
primitives.breakdown_regime: High uncertainty regions where optimal policies disagree

layer2.mapping: GSE situational reasoning: abstain when posterior predictive intervals overlap beyond a threshold, preserving coverage while maximizing expected value.
layer2.telemetry: Post-abstention selective ROI on held-out test data, compared to a fixed baseline policy

primitives.name: Doubly-Robust Pseudo-Outcomes
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Unknown propensities (§3.2, Algorithm 4):** replace IPW with doubly-robust pseudo-outcomes φ̂(x,d,y) = ĝ(d,x) + [dD/p̂(x) + (1-d)(1-D)/(1-p̂(x))](y - ĝ(d,x)); same construction with expanded α.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: ŷ-hat: outcome estimate (same units as Y), p-hat: propensity estimate (dimensionless), φ-hat: pseudo-outcome (same units as Y)
primitives.assumptions: Overlap (propensity bounded away from 0 and 1), consistent nuisance models g(d,x) and p(x)
primitives.breakdown_regime: Near-extreme propensities where inverse-propensity weighting becomes unstable

layer2.mapping: GSI conformal prediction: use a machine learning model to predict centered outcomes (residuals) and add them to a point forecast, yielding valid predictive intervals without distributional assumptions.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error on the pseudo-outcomes, evaluated out-of-sample

primitives.name: Abstention Bonus p
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model **Framework:** abstention earns reward (Y(1)+Y(0))/2 + p — the value of a random guess plus a small fixed bonus p ≥ 0.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p: fixed abstention bonus (same units as reward Y), v(π,x): conditional value of action π(x), V(p): expected abstaining value
primitives.assumptions: Bounded rewards Y ∈ [0,1], known baseline value (Y(1)+Y(0))/2
primitives.breakdown_regime: p → 0+ (small bonus shrinks the incentive to abstain)

layer2.mapping: GSE post/no-post decision: set p equal to the expected profit margin per accepted bet, balancing the cost of wrong abstentions against the benefit of correct abstentions.
layer2.telemetry: Total profit on accepted picks, net of costs associated with abstaining on losing bets

primitives.name: Safe Policy Improvement Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT The disagreement-based abstention construction (abstain exactly where near-optimal policies disagree) and the abstention-powered safe-policy-improvement protocol are both directly adaptable: the first to GSE's post/no-post decision, the second to certifying engine version upgrades before public deployment.
primitives.assumptions: Independent test set, valid confidence bounds, baseline policy with known value
primitives.breakdown_regime: Test set size insufficient to distinguish between policies with similar empirical performance

layer2.mapping: GSE engine upgrade certification: treat the candidate engine as a new policy, construct a one-sided lower confidence bound on its value relative to the current production engine, and deploy only if the bound exceeds a regulatory threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Pass/Fail decision based on whether the lower confidence bound crosses zero
